source_snapshot.instance_inventory_rule: All 50 .gph graph files in 07-independentset/instances at the pinned commit; README.md intentionally excluded.
source_snapshot.hashes: git_blob_sha1 records are Git object IDs, not SHA-256 digests of raw file bytes. The immutable repository commit pins these records.

comparability_warnings: The QOBLIB graph README states that several DIMACS graphs have already been inverted from max-clique instances to independent-set instances. Never complement these entries a second time. Read the pinned README before building QUBO mappings.
The official solution checker validates independent-set feasibility but does not certify optimality. Preserve exact/best-known objective provenance separately.

QOBLIB leaderboard totals are not matched head-to-head runtime or cost comparisons. Symthaea experiments must rerun all selected policies on the same instances under preregistered resource boundaries.

development_partition.purpose: grouped family-held-out development split for selector/model development
development_partition.assignment_rule: Deterministic grouping from source name prefixes / recognizable benchmark families; all instances sharing a named family remain within one split; otherwise each graph is a singleton family.
limitations: This is not a blinded test set: QOBLIB instances and best-known results are public, and published records may have influenced prior development.
Family groups are provisional source-name groupings, not proof of independent graph-generation distributions.
Use this partition to audit family leakage, not to claim out-of-distribution generalization without additional newly generated and independently frozen families.
The split is immutable for this cohort revision; any changes require a new partition ID and explicit rationale.
Singleton-named families are kept distinct; one-off names do not imply a coherent generative family.

paper.title: Quantum-informed reduction algorithm for the maximum independent set problem
paper.note: Published paper claims are external references, not independently reproduced results from Symthaea.

workload.upstream_description: Random unit-disk instances with Union-Jack connectivity, radius sqrt(2), density 0.8, varying grid length L and seeds, as described by the pinned upstream results README.
workload.intended_track: Paper-reproduction and transfer track, kept separate from QOBLIB's 50 heterogeneous MIS graphs.
workload.published_scale_context: Paper reports hardware experiments up to 231 qubits; this is context, not a Symthaea result.
workload.ground_truth_method: Pinned upstream README says MIS ground truth was computed by a sweeping-line algorithm; independently verify the corresponding solution/bound artifacts before consuming them.

paper_arms.qReduMIS: Quantum-informed classical reduction; the pinned upstream README describes 20 classical shots, in-set selection, and no fixed depth/iteration limit in the paper's extensive experiment protocol.
paper_arms.randomReduMIS: Replaces the quantum-informed in-set choice with a random pick for the same number of classical iterations, as described by the pinned upstream README.
paper_arms.simulatedAnnealing: The published paper also reports a matched classical simulated-annealing comparison. A replication must pin its exact code/configuration and resource accounting rather than infer them from this summary.

execution_conventions.postprocessing: Pinned README describes removal/addition fixup for backend counts and additional loading-error postprocessing for hardware data.
execution_conventions.dependency_note: The pinned upstream instructions require Python 3.9 and a custom Amazon Braket tensor-network simulator branch for some simulator reproduction. Treat this as an isolated external reproduction environment, not a Symthaea production dependency.
execution_conventions.source_artifact_gap: The pinned results README references generator/generate.py, but no file at that path was present in the inspected pinned repository tree. Do not claim a generator-based recreation until its exact source is located or graph coordinates/parameters are independently frozen.

comparison_gates: Record exact graph coordinate bytes, input parameters, random seed and SHA-256 digest for every UJ instance.
Separate published raw hardware receipts, newly executed QPU output, tensor-network simulation, and postprocessed replay.
Match reducer implementation, in-set/out-set selection policy, iteration budget, candidate/shot budget, postprocessing and stopping conditions across arms.
Report success probability and cost-to-target together; count all classical and hardware costs and retries.
Run a separate comparison against randomReduMIS and strong classical local-search/solver-population informers.
Do not pool this graph family with the QOBLIB cohort or claim state-of-the-art from a cross-paper comparison.

literature.title: Scalable quantum-enhanced greedy algorithm for maximum independent set problems on random regular graphs

repositories_searched: GitHub repository search for paper title and authors
GitHub code search for random regular graphs / QAOA-enhanced greedy MIS
official_implementation_search.result: No matching official source repository for this paper surfaced in the searches performed on 2026-10-24.
official_implementation_search.consequence: Do not claim reproduction of the paper's implementation until official code or a clearly justified independent reimplementation is pinned. Any Symthaea reimplementation must have its own branch/commit, test oracle and fixed-angle source table, and must be labelled independently implemented.

workload.graph_sizes: The paper's Section IV text says 10^5 random 3-regular graph instances for each size in the SOTA comparison, while the Fig. 3 caption says 200 instances for QGreedy at each plotted size (100 for the p=3 hardware case) with N=50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000. Treat the exact sample count for each reported result as unresolved until the authors' data/supplement clarifies which curves use which cohort. The paper reports statistically significant p=4 gains against the prioritized baseline for considered sizes through N<=2000 and discusses p=4 results to about N=5000.
workload.statistical_unit: graph instance; if multiple seeds/solver repetitions are run on one graph, treat them as nested repetitions
workload.keep_separate_from: QOBLIB's heterogeneous 50-instance named graph cohort and qReduMIS random unit-disk / Union-Jack cohort

methods.standard_minimum_degree_greedy: Minimum-degree selection with random choice among equal-degree candidates; retain a stable/index-tie implementation as a separate control.
methods.classical_sota: Marino-Kirkpatrick linear-prioritized local search for random d-regular graphs; source paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12293. Reproduce its virtual-node/contraction rules, tie handling and stopping conditions exactly before calling it the SOTA baseline.
methods.quantum_informed: Precomputed fixed-angle QAOA local expectation values guide choices among eligible minimum-degree vertices; the paper uses tree-derived angles and studies depths p=1..4.
methods.negative_control: Randomized tie breaking with matched candidate sets and the same number of classical greedy decisions
methods.source_paper_simulation: Tensor-network simulations; keep approximate simulation evidence separately labelled from physical QPU data

required_metrics: mean independent-set ratio |I|/|V| by graph size, with raw per-instance outcomes
paired delta against both plain minimum-degree greedy and Marino-Kirkpatrick linear-prioritized search
feasibility rate and run failures; never drop invalid sets
uncertainty intervals and multiplicity handling for the preregistered size/depth family
end-to-end wall time, classical runtime, QPU runtime, shots, candidate expectations, circuit batches, recalculation/cache counts, and all-in cost under explicit boundaries
target-hit probability and time-to-target if a fixed cardinality/ratio target is preregistered
execution_gates: Resolve the paper's Section IV versus Figure 3 caption sample-count discrepancy using official raw data, supplement or author clarification; freeze an exact per-curve n before replication.
Pin exact graph generator source, version, degree, random seeds and byte-level graph digests; verify every generated graph is simple, connectedness policy is declared, and every vertex has degree 3.
Reproduce fixed QAOA angle tables from a pinned paper appendix/reference and record the exact depth-angle mapping; don't tune angles on the confirmatory test instances.
Implement the classical linear-prioritized baseline independently and cross-check its contraction sequence/outputs against the paper's description or author's code if found.
Run the standard greedy, randomized tie, linear-prioritized and QAOA-informed arms on the exact same graph instances and instance-level seeds.
Keep physical hardware, ideal circuit simulation, tensor-network simulation, and emulated/replayed observations as separate evidence classes.
For the main confirmatory claim, freeze metrics and multiplicity handling before generating or evaluating the test graphs.
Do not pool results with QOBLIB or qReduMIS random unit-disk instances; do not infer general MIS SOTA from random 3-regular graph evidence.
current_gaps: Official code repository for the October 2026 accepted paper was not found in the GitHub searches performed; reproduction is not yet possible from a verified official implementation.

The source paper claims statistically significant improvement over its classical prioritized search for considered sizes up to N <= 2000, and reports results up to about N≈5000 for p=4; those are paper results, not Symthaea results.
Full hardware cost boundary, QPU queue/compilation conventions and raw trial artifacts must be frozen before cross-method operational-cost comparisons.

The accepted-paper text has an apparent sample-count discrepancy: Section IV states 10^5 instances per size for the SOTA comparison, while Fig. 3's caption describes 200 QGreedy instances per depth/size (100 for hardware p=3). Reproduction must resolve rather than silently choose one.

reported_sample_count_discrepancy.primary_text: Section IV states 10^5 random 3-regular graph instances for each system size in the SOTA comparison.
reported_sample_count_discrepancy.figure_caption: Figure 3 says 200 graph instances for QGreedy for each p (100 for the p=3 IQM Garnet series) and lists N=50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000.
reported_sample_count_discrepancy.protocol_rule: Do not choose one count as the authoritative reproduction target without checking source data, supplementary materials, or an author clarification. Record separate per-curve counts and raw instance digests in any replication.

complete_baseline_inventory.caveat: Published external records only; not a Symthaea run or controlled cross-hardware comparison.

last_research_note: Added a separate random-3-regular QAOA-enhanced greedy reproduction track. Bare minimum-degree greedy is not the sufficient classical SOTA comparison on regular graphs: include Marino-Kirkpatrick linear-prioritized search. No official repository surfaced in the source search, so reproduction remains planned and no paper result is claimed.
